items.title: [Bug] CUDA graph causes garbled outputs with concurrent multi-LoRA decoding on GLM-5.1-FP8
items.body:
### Checklist

- [ ] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [ ] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [ ] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [ ] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

# CUDA graph causes garbled outputs with concurrent multi-LoRA decoding on GLM-5.1-FP8

## Summary

We found a reproducible output corruption issue when serving GLM-5.1-FP8 with multiple LoRA adapters and CUDA graph enabled. Under concurrent decode, most requests collapse into repeated `!` tokens, while disabling CUDA graph makes the same workload clean.

This reproduces on clean upstream SGLang without any local patch/overlay.





### Reproduction

## Launch Command

Example with 5 LoRAs and CUDA graph enabled:

```bash
export PYTHONPATH=/sgl-workspace/sglang/python

python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /path/to/GLM-5.1-FP8 \
  --served-model-name zai-org/glm-5.1 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 30000 \
  --tp 8 \
  --reasoning-parser glm45 \
  --tool-call-parser glm47 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.93 \
  --enable-metrics \
  --enable-mfu-metrics \
  --disable-custom-all-reduce \
  --enable-lora \
  --lora-paths \
    r0_random=/path/to/random_loras/R0 \
    r1_random=/path/to/random_loras/R1 \
    r2_random=/path/to/random_loras/R2 \
    r3_random=/path/to/random_loras/R3 \
    r4_random=/path/to/random_loras/R4 \
  --max-loaded-loras 5 \
  --max-loras-per-batch 2 \
  --max-lora-rank 16 \
  --lora-use-virtual-experts \
  --disable-overlap-schedule \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs 16
```

Control run:

```bash
# Same command, but replace --cuda-graph-max-bs 16 with:
--disable-cuda-graph
```

## Reproduction Script

```python
import json
import urllib.request
import concurrent.futures

BASE = "http://127.0.0.1:30000"
PROMPT = "Write three sentences about the ocean."
MODELS = ["r0_random", "r1_random", "r2_random", "r3_random", "r4_random"]

N = 16
MAX_TOKENS = 128

def call(i):
    model = MODELS[i % len(MODELS)]
    body = json.dumps({
        "model": model,
        "prompt": PROMPT,
        "max_tokens": MAX_TOKENS,
        "temperature": 0
    }).encode()

    req = urllib.request.Request(
        BASE + "/v1/completions",
        data=body,
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
    )

    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=240) as r:
        d = json.loads(r.read())

    text = d["choices"][0]["text"]
    finish_reason = d["choices"][0].get("finish_reason")
    bad = ("!!!!!" in text) or (text.count("!") >= 20)

    return i, model, finish_reason, bad, text.count("!"), text[-100:]

with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=N) as ex:
    rows = sorted(ex.map(call, range(N)))

for i, model, fin, bad, bangs, tail in rows:
    print(f"[req#{i:02d}] {model} fin={fin} "
          f"{GARBLED if bad else clean} bangs={bangs} tail={tail!r}")

print("SUMMARY garbled=%d total=%d" % (
    sum(1 for row in rows if row[3]), len(rows)
))
```

## Actual Result

With CUDA graph enabled, most concurrent requests collapse into repeated `!` tokens.

Example:

```text
[req#00] r0_random fin=length clean   bangs=0
[req#01] r1_random fin=length GARBLED bangs=70 tail=" the oceans density!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
[req#02] r2_random fin=length GARBLED bangs=70 tail= the oceans density!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!"
...
SUMMARY garbled=15 total=16
```

## Control Result

With `--disable-cuda-graph`, the same workload is clean:

```text
SUMMARY garbled=0 total=16
```

## Test Matrix

We tested randomly initialized LoRAs from 2 to 6 adapters. All use the same server settings except CUDA graph on/off.

| Random LoRA count | CUDA graph on | CUDA graph off |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 2 | 15/16 garbled | 0/16 garbled |
| 3 | 15/16 garbled | 0/16 garbled |
| 4 | 15/16 garbled | 0/16 garbled |
| 5 | 15/16 garbled | 0/16 garbled |
| 6 | 15/16 garbled | 0/16 garbled |

We also reproduced this with 5 trained LoRAs:

| LoRA type | CUDA graph on | CUDA graph off |
|---|---:|---:|
| 5 trained LoRAs | 15/16 garbled | 0/16 garbled |

## Notes

The random LoRAs were initialized with valid PEFT LoRA structure, rank 16, same target modules as the trained adapters. We used small random `lora_A` weights and zero `lora_B`, so the adapters are effectively near no-op. The corruption still reproduces, which suggests the issue is not caused by LoRA training quality or adapter content.

The key observation is that greedy decoding with `temperature=0` and identical prompts should be deterministic and consistent across requests. Instead, with CUDA graph enabled, most batch slots collapse into repeated `!` tokens. Disabling CUDA graph removes the issue.

This looks like a CUDA graph replay / static buffer / batch-slot state corruption issue in concurrent decode with multi-LoRA enabled, possibly related to GLM-5.1 FP8 + DSA decode backend (`fa3`) and LoRA CUDA graph buffers.


### Environment

## Environment

- SGLang: 0.5.13
- Model: `zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8`
- TP: 8
- GPUs: 8x GPU, each ~144GB memory
- KV cache dtype/backend observed in logs:
  - `Set DSA backends for bfloat16 KV Cache: prefill=flashmla_sparse, decode=fa3`
- LoRA:
  - `--enable-lora`
  - `--lora-use-virtual-experts`
  - `--max-lora-rank 16`
  - `--max-loras-per-batch 2`
  - tested with 2-6 LoRA adapters
- Clean SGLang source only:
  - `PYTHONPATH=/sgl-workspace/sglang/python`
  - no local monkey patch / overlay loaded

items.title: [Bug] A non-object entry in a tool-call array discards the valid calls beside it
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

When a tool-call array contains an entry that is valid JSON but not an object, the valid tool calls beside it are silently discarded.

```
[{"name": "get_weather", "arguments": {"city": "Paris"}}, "junk"]
  -> no tool calls at all, though the first entry is a well-formed call
```

The model asked for the weather correctly; that request is lost because an unrelated entry sat next to it in the array. No crafted input is needed — only a model emitting a slightly malformed array, which is ordinary behaviour.

### Cause

`BaseFormatDetector.parse_base_json` reads `act.get("name")` without checking that `act` is an object (`python/sglang/srt/function_call/base_format_detector.py:83`):

```python
results = []
for act in action:
    name = act.get("name")
```

A non-object entry raises `AttributeError`:

```
[1, 2]   -> AttributeError: 'int' object has no attribute 'get'
["x"]    -> AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'get'
[null]   -> AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get'
[[]]     -> AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get'
```

On the chat path `serving_chat.py:2145` catches that and returns `ToolCallProcessingResult(None, ...)`, dropping every call in the response.

This looks like a missed branch rather than absent error handling: the same function already defines what to do with an unusable entry a few lines below, and it is not "abort the batch" —

```python
if not (name and name in tool_indices):
    logger.warning(f"Model attempted to call undefined function: {name}")
    if not envs.SGLANG_FORWARD_UNKNOWN_TOOLS.get():
        continue  # skip this entry, keep the rest
```

An unknown tool name is skipped and parsing continues. A non-object entry should behave the same way.

### Secondary: `/parse_function_call` returns HTTP 500

The same `AttributeError` reaches the HTTP layer uncaught. `/parse_function_call` (`http_server.py:1632`) passes `obj.text` straight from the request body to `parse_non_stream` with no `try/except` — unlike `/abort_request` above it. `parse_non_stream` (`function_call_parser.py:138`) has no guard either, and the only registered exception handlers are for `HTTPException` and `RequestValidationError`, so it reaches Starlette's default handler.

That half is arguably just error handling — the input is malformed and rejecting it is correct. It is included because it is the quickest way to observe the exception, and because a 500 is the wrong way to reject a well-formed request.

### Scope

Reproduced through `FunctionCallParser.parse_non_stream()` for `qwen25`, `llama3`, `mistral` and `trinity`. Detectors with their own `try/except` (e.g. `hermes`, `deepseekv3`) are unaffected.

The discarded-valid-call effect applies to parsers whose payload between the markers is itself a JSON array (`qwen25`, `trinity`). `llama3` separates calls with `;` and mistral's `[` is part of its `bot_token`, so neither accepts an array there — for those two the uncaught exception is the only effect.

---


### Reproduction



```python
from sglang.srt.entrypoints.openai.protocol import Function, Tool
from sglang.srt.function_call.function_call_parser import FunctionCallParser

tools = [Tool(type="function", function=Function(
    name="get_weather", parameters={"type": "object", "properties": {}}))]

parser = FunctionCallParser(tools=tools, tool_call_parser="qwen25")

# the valid call is lost because of the entry beside it
parser.parse_non_stream(
    '<tool_call>\n[{"name": "get_weather", "arguments": {"city": "Paris"}}, "junk"]\n</tool_call>'
)
# AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'get'

# minimal form
parser.parse_non_stream('<tool_call>\n[1, 2]\n</tool_call>')
# AttributeError: 'int' object has no attribute 'get'
```

Against a running server:

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:30000/parse_function_call \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"text": "<tool_call>\n[1, 2]\n</tool_call>",
       "tool_call_parser": "qwen25",
       "tools": [{"type": "function",
                  "function": {"name": "get_weather",
                               "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {}}}}]}'
```

items.title: [Bug] Scheduler event loop blocks on Mamba eviction under large-context requests, causing server hang and process kill
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

When serving a hybrid Mamba model with hierarchical cache enabled, the SGLang scheduler's event loop intermittently blocks for over 3 minutes, making the server unresponsive to `/health` checks and all incoming requests. This leads to process termination (SIGKILL) by the container runtime.

1. **Silent event loop hang**: The server stops responding with no error in logs. The last logged request completes normally, then no further log output appears. Metrics scrape returns empty until the process is killed and restarted.

2. **Long TTFT stall before hang**: A single request exhibits **222-second TTFT** (`e2e_latency: 225s`), during which the scheduler is blocked and cannot process `/health` or any other request. After this request completes, the server receives SIGTERM and shuts down.

In both cases:
- No OOM, no CUDA error, no `AssertionError`, no NaN in logs
- `mamba_available_tokens = 0` with `mamba_evictable_tokens ≈ 68` (free-list empty but evictable slots exist)

### Reproduction

The issue is intermittent and requires production-scale traffic to reproduce. However, the conditions that trigger it are:

1. Hybrid Mamba model with hierarchical cache enabled
2. `mamba_available_tokens` drops to 0 (free-list exhausted)
3. `mamba_evictable_tokens > 0` (eviction is attempted)
4. A large-context request arrives (e.g., 100K+ tokens)
5. Scheduler blocks on eviction I/O → `/health` timeout → process kill

### Environment

- **SGLang version**: v0.5.14
- **Model**: Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 (hybrid Mamba), TP=8
- **Hardware**: H100 80GB × 8 per replica
- **Launch command**:

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
```

items.title: [Bug] MiniMax-M3 tool-call parser: top-level `oneOf` parameters schema not resolved (numbers become strings, arrays leak raw tags)
items.body:
## Checklist
- [x] Searched existing issues
- [x] Reproduced on latest main

## Describe the bug

When a tool's `parameters` uses a top-level `oneOf` (a common JSON-Schema composition), SGLang's
MiniMax-M3 tool-call parser fails to resolve the per-branch property schemas. As a result the emitted
`tool_calls[].function.arguments` have the wrong types:

- a `number` argument is returned as a **string** (`{"number": "42"}` instead of `{"number": 42}`)
- an `array` argument **leaks the model's raw internal parser tags** as a plain string
  (`{"stringList": "]<]minimax[>[<item>12]<]minimax[>[</item>..."}` instead of `{"stringList": ["12","34"]}`)

This is caught by MiniMax's official verifier test
`m3_format_check/m3_text_tests.py::TestToolCallSchema::test_14_07_oneof_toplevel_schema_stream`.

## Reproduction

Serve MiniMax-M3 with tool-call parsing enabled:

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --reasoning-parser auto \
  --tool-call-parser auto \
  --tp-size 4 \
  --port 8043
```

Run the official verifier test (from https://github.com/MiniMax-AI/MiniMax-Provider-Verifier):

```bash
export M3_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8043
export M3_API_KEY=sk-none
export M3_MODEL=MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3
cd m3_format_check
python3 -m pytest \
  "m3_text_tests.py::TestToolCallSchema::test_14_07_oneof_toplevel_schema_stream" -v
```

The test defines a tool whose `parameters` is a top-level `oneOf` with three branches
(`number` / `stringList` / `numberList`) and asks the model to call it three times, once per branch,
with `number=42`, `stringList=["12","34"]`, `numberList=[12,34]`.

## Actual behavior (official verifier output)

```
m3_text_tests.py::TestToolCallSchema::test_14_07_oneof_toplevel_schema_stream FAILED

E   AssertionError: oneof toplevel stream: number must be numeric, got str='42'.
    calls=[
      {'name': 'ExampleFunction', 'arguments_raw': '{"number": "42"}'},
      {'name': 'ExampleFuumber": "42"}'},
      {'name': 'ExampleFunction', 'arguments_raw': '{"stringList": "]<]minimax[>[<item>12]<]minimax[>[</item>]<]minimax[>[<item>34]<]minimax[>[</item>"}'},
      {'name': 'ExampleFunction', 'arguments_raw': '{"numberList": "]<]minimax[>[<item>12]<]minimax[>[</item>]<]minimax[>[<item>34]<]minimax[>[</item>"}'}
    ]
```

- `number` → `"42"` (string, should be `42`)
- `stringList` / `numberList` → a string containing raw `]<]minimax[>[<item>...` tags
  (should be `["12","34"]` and `[12,34]`)

## Expected behavior

```json
{"number": 42}
{"stringList": ["12", "34"]}
{"numberList": [12, 34]}
```

## Environment

- SGresent on current main)
- Model: `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3`

```
ValueError: The checkpoint you are trying to load has model type `glm5_next` but Transformers does not recognize this architecture. This could be because of an issue with the checkpoint, or because your version of Transformers is out of date.
You can update Transformers with the command `pip install --upgrade transformers`. If this does not work, and the checkpoint is very new, then there may not be a release version that supports this model yet. In this case, you can get the most up‑to‑date code by installing Transformers from source with the command `pip install git+https://github.com/huggingface/transformers.git`
```

### Root cause analysis (my observation)

The model `config.json` contains `"model_type": "glm5_next"`.
In v0.5.18 release image, `AutoConfig.from_pretrained()` runs **before** `--trust-remote-code` takes effect during the early config‑resolution pipeline (`_apply_inkling_prefill_cuda_graph_default`). Therefore transformers cannot recognize `glm5_next` and throws error, even though `--trust‑remote‑code` is passed.
The cookbook page uses main‑branch nightly image (`rocm/sgl-dev`) instead of the tagged release `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.18‑rocm720‑mi30x`.

### Questions

1. Is `glm5_next` supposed to be supported in v0.5.18 release?
2. Is there a workaround without upgrading transformers inside container or modifying model config.json?

items.title: [Bug] HiCache prefetch all_reduce deadlock with TP=4, no PP — mismatched call count in check_prefetch_progress
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] 1. I have searched related issues but cannot get the expected help.
- [x] 2. The bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] 3. Please note that if the bug-related issue you submitted lacks corresponding environment info and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be challenging for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, reducing the likelihood of receiving feedback.
- [x] 4. If the issue you raised is not a bug but a question, please raise a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions/new/choose Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] 5. Please use English, otherwise it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

Originally reported this under #22607, but per @stepinto that issue/#27010 is specifically about **PP** rank divergence (`loading_check`/`writing_check` completion-event counts). This deployment is **TP-only** (`tp_size=4, pp_size=1, dp_size=1, ep_size=1` — no PP at all), so opening as a separate issue with full server args as requested.

The scheduler deadlocks with one TP rank stuck forever in an `all_reduce` inside HiCache's prefetch-completion check, while the other TP ranks have already moved on to the next scheduling iteration and will never come back to answer it. GPU utilization for the affected TP group drops to 0% and never recovers; there is no automatic recovery.

**Stack (rank 0 / TP0):**
```
all_reduce (torch/distributed/distributed_c10d.py:3075)
  _all_reduce_attn_groups (hiradix_cache.py:196)
  can_terminate_prefetch (hiradix_cache.py:1350)
  check_prefetch_progress (hiradix_cache.py:1373)
  _get_new_batch_prefill_raw (scheduler.py:2679)
  get_new_batch_prefill (scheduler.py:2558)
  get_next_batch_to_run (scheduler.py:2498)
  event_loop_overlap (scheduler.py:1471)
```

**Stack (TP1 / TP2 / TP3, identical):**
```
broadcast (torch/distributed/distributed_c10d.py:2974)
  broadcast_pyobj (utils/common.py:1437)
  _broadcast_reqs_across_ranks (scheduler_components/request_receiver.py:187)
  recv_requests (scheduler_components/request_receiver.py:87)
  event_loop_overlap (scheduler.py:1461)
```

Rank 0 is one loop iteration behind the others, still inside the batch-building loop:

```python
# scheduler.py, _get_new_batch_prefill_raw
for req in self.waiting_queue:
    if self.running_batch.batch_is_full:
        break                          # per-rank local capacity check
    if self.enable_hicache_storage:
        prefetch_done = self.tree_cache.check_prefetch_progress(req.rid)   # -> all_reduce
```

`check_prefetch_progress` → `can_terminate_prefetch` unconditionally calls `_all_reduce_attn_groups` once per candidate request examined, and the loop's exit condition (`batch_is_full`) is computed independently per rank from local KV-cache/allocator state. On this occurrence, rank 0 examined one more candidate request than ranks 1-3 before its own `batch_is_full` check tripped, so it called the collective one more time than they did — a straightforward call-count mismatch, permanent hang.

Verified this is not a slow-prefetch / storage-latency issue: rank 0's own background prefetch thread had already completed the exact same operation (same `PrefetchOperation` object, same `hash_value`, same `storage_hit_count`) that ranks 1-3's prefetch threads had also just finished, at the same wall-clock time. The divergence is in scheduling/control-flow (`batch_is_full`), not in mooncake I/O.

Also confirmed not a hardware issue: `DCGM_FI_DEV_XID_ERRORS` was 0 on every GPU for the whole window, and all 4 processes were in Linux state `S` (interruptible sleep) with `py-spy` attaching cleanly.

Separately, the scheduler's own hard watchdog never fired to auto-recover this hang, because `create_scheduler_watchdog`'s `is_active` gates on `scheduler.cur_batch is not None`, and this hang occurs before a batch is chosen (`cur_batch` still `None`). Happy to open that as its own issue if useful, flagging it here since it's why this required a manual restart instead of self-healing.

### Reproduction

No minimal repro script yet — this surfaced on a long-running production deployment under real traffic, not from a targeted stress test. Full launch command and parsed `ServerArgs` below. Can dig further / pull more `py-spy` dumps if that's useful, but wanted to get the environment + stacks filed per your request rather than sit on it.

Launch command (from `docker top` at the time of the hang):

```
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /data/GLM-5.2-FP8 \
  --served-model-name glm-5-fp8-200k \
  --tp 4 \
  --reasoning-parser glm45 --tool-call-parser glm47 \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 3 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \
  --max-prefill-tokens 65536 --page-size 64 \
  --enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-ratio 2 --hicache-size 128 \
  --hicache-io-backend kernel --hicache-mem-layout page_first \
  --hicache-write-policy write_through_selective \
  --hicache-storage-backend mooncake \
  --hicache-storage-prefetch-policy timeout \
  --hicache-storage-backend-extra-config '{"master_server_address":"<redacted>:50051","metadata_server":"P2PHANDSHAKE","protocol":"rdma","device_name":"mlx5_5,mlx5_10,mlx5_11,mlx5_12","local_hostname":"<redacted>","global_segment_size":"64gb"}' \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.9 --max-queued-requests 3 \
  --disable-custom-all-reduce --enable-metrics --enable-cache-report \
  --dist-init-addr 127.0.0.1:8334 --nccl-port 38389 \
  --engine-info-bootstrap-port 6790 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8001
```

Relevant fields from the parsed `ServerArgs` at startup (same deployment, redeployed after this incident — hicache sizing was retuned afterward, everything else matches):

```
tp_size=4, pp_size=1, dp_size=1, ep_size=1, attn_cp_size=1
attention_backend='dsa', moe_runner_backend='flashinfer_trtllm', speculative_moe_runner_backend='flashinfer_trtllm'
fp8_gemm_runner_backend='auto', speculative_algorithm='EAGLE'
enable_hierarchical_cache=True, hicache_write_policy='write_through_selective'
hicache_io_backend='kernel', hicache_mem_layout='page_first'
hicache_storage_prefetch_policy='timeout'
watchdog_timeout=300, soft_watchdog_timeout=None
disable_custom_all_reduce=True
```

### Environment

```
sglang: 0.5.13.post1
torch: 2.11.0+cu130
GPU: NVIDIA, 4x for this replica
Model: GLM-5.2-FP8
Parallelism: tp_size=4, pp_size=1, dp_size=1, ep_size=1 (TP only)
```

Related: #10070 (closed — near-identical stack signature, `all_reduce` inside `hiradix_cache.py` reached from `get_new_batch_prefill`, but no repro confirmed there either). #22607 / #27010 — same general failure shape (rank divergence around HiCache async completion tracking causing a collective mismatch) but for **PP**, not applicable here per @stepinto.

### Describe the bug

## Describe the bug

Enabling `--enable-dp-attention` on GPT-OSS-120B (MXFP4) with `--tp 4 --dp 4 --ep 4 --moe-a2a-backend none` completely breaks generation, while the identical command without DP attention works fine.

With DP attention on, responses are dominated by repeated Harmony channel markers, empty final answers, and runaway generation that hits the 8192-token cap. Fixed-prompt evals (temperature 0, seed 4242):

| | GSM8K (first 128, 5-shot) | MMLU (fixed 128 subset) |
|---|---|---|
| DP attention off | 124/128 (96.9%) | 110/128 (85.9%) |
| DP attention on | **0/128 (0%)** | **4/128 (3.1%)** |

The problem is not specific to chunk size, MoE runner backend (`flashinfer_mxfp4` or `triton`), CUDA graph, overlap schedule, radix cache, or hybrid SWA KV pool — we tried toggling each one alone and none recovered basic QA. Also reproducible on current `main` by source inspection; the GPU repro below was on v0.5.18.



### Reproduction

Official image `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.18`, model `openai/gpt-oss-120b`:

```bash

  --model-path openai/gpt-oss-120b \
  --tp 4 --dp 4 --ep 4 --moe-a2a-backend none \
  --quantization mxfp4 --dtype bfloat16 \
  --attention-backend trtllm_mha --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.85 --max-total-tokens 1048576 --max-prefill-tokens 131072 \
  --context-length 65536 --disable-prefill-cuda-graph --disable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --random-seed 4242 --cuda-graph-max-bs 128 --max-running-requests 512 \
  --disable-radix-cache --reasoning-parser gpt-oss --tool-call-parser gpt-oss \
  --chunked-prefill-size 65536 --enable-dp-attention
```

The control (working) run is the same command with `--dp 4 --enable-dp-attention` removed and `--chunked-prefill-size 16384` (both land at an effective chunk of 16384 per rank). Eval via the OpenAI-compatible API with temperature 0, top_p 1, seed 4242, `reasoning_effort=low`, max_tokens 8192, concurrency 128; ask something trivial like "What is 2+2? Reply with only the number." — the DP-attention server returns channel-marker gibberish or an empty final answer.

items.title: [Bug] Qwen3.8-Flash-Next W4A16 on A100 TP4: Marlin MoE invalid thread config; Triton MoE then hits QSA FA-CuTe capture failure
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest day-0 image.
- [x] This report includes environment info and reproduction parameters.
- [x] This is a bug report, not a general question.

### Summary

On 4x NVIDIA A100-40GB with TP4, the day-0 `qwen38flashnext` image can load the community W4A16 checkpoint of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next with PLE host offload and bundled NEXTN/MTP. Startup fails at CUDA-graph capture, but with two independent kernel failures depending on the MoE runner backend:

1. Default/auto MoE: `CompressedTensorsWNA16MarlinMoEMethod` throws `Invalid thread config` for the TP4 expert GEMM shape `MKN = [64, 2560, 320]`.
2. `--moe-runner-backend triton` selects `CompressedTensorsWNA16TritonMoE` successfully and avoids the Marlin error, but QSA sparse attention then falls into `flash_attn.cute` during CUDA-graph capture and fails with an MLIR `crd2idx` compilation error.

The second run also emits many Triton warnings similar to:

```text
Data race detected: `Logits(bx, position)` is written by multiple threads in loop (token,)
```

### Environment

```text
GPU: 4x NVIDIA A100-SXM4/PCIe 40GB (TP4)
Driver-visible model names: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB, NVIDIA A100-PCIE-40GB
Model: /data/ai/models/vllm/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-W4A16 (compressed-tensors W4A16)
Image: lmsysorg/sglang:qwen38flashnext
Image digest: sha256:4175343ed77bb05000ee5019b2dc3fa8999cd52edd6da7e5b75d23306c445c5f
CUDA in container: 13.0.3
TP: 4
Host RAM: 377 GiB (PLE offload fits comfortably)
```

### Reproduction

The model was mounted at `/models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-W4A16`. This is the minimum command structure used with Docker Compose:

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-W4A16 \
  --ple-offload-embedding \
  --speculative-algorithm NEXTN \
  --speculative-num-steps 3 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \
  --moe-runner-backend auto \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8888 \
  --tp 4 \
  --context-length 262144 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.95 \
  --attention-backend flashinfer \
  --chunked-prefill-size 16384 \
  --max-prefill-tokens 32768 \
  --max-running-requests 16 \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs 16 \
  --cuda-graph-bs-prefill 4 8 16 32 64 128 256 512 1024 2048 4096 8192 16384 \
  --schedule-policy fcfs \
  --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder \
  --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
  --served-model-name Qwen3.8-Flash-Next \
  --dtype bfloat16 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --mamba-ssm-dtype float32 \
  --mamba-backend flashinfer \
  --mm-feature-transport cpu \
  --disable-custom-all-reduce
```

For the second failure, replace `--moe-runner-backend auto` with:

```bash
--moe-runner-backend triton
```

### Result 1 — default/auto: Marlin MoE shape/thread-config failure

Model and MTP weights load successfully. During decode CUDA-graph capture:

```text
[TP0] Using CompressedTensorsWNA16MarlinMoEMethod
...
Capturing batches (bs=16 avail_mem=2.10 GB):   0%| 0/12 [00:00<?, ?it/s]
tvm.error.InternalError: Failed at .../moe_wna16_marlin.cuh:747:
Invalid thread config: thread_m_blocks = 1, thread_k = -1, thread_n = -1,
num_threads = -1 for MKN = [64, 2560, 320] and num_bits = 4,
group_size = 128, has_act_order = 0, is_k_full = 1, has_zp = 0,
is_zp_float = 0, max_shared_mem = 166912
```

Relevant stack:

```text
fused_moe_triton/layer.py -> run_moe_core
compressed_tensors.py -> scheme.apply_weights
compressed_tensors_wNa16_moe.py -> fused_marlin_moe
moe_wna16_marlin.py -> module.moe_wna16_marlin_gemm
moe_wna16_marlin.cuh -> host::RuntimeCheck(is_valid_config(...))
```

Observations:

- `MKN = [64, 2560, 320]` appears to be one of the TP4-sharded expert GEMMs.
- The small `prob_n = 320` is not divisible by the 128-wide tile candidate, so both built-in small-batch configs are rejected.
- The error occurs before service readiness; there is no OOM.

### Result 2 — `--moe-runner-backend triton`: Marlin is bypassed, but QSA/FA-CuTe capture fails

Logs confirm the intended switch:

```text
Using CompressedTensorsWNA16TritonMoE (moe_runner_backend=triton)
```

There are also missing tuned-kernel notices for A100:

```text
Using default MoE kernel config. Performance might be sub-optimal!
Config file not found:
.../E=512,N=80,device_name=NVIDIA_A100-SXM4-40GB,dtype=int4_w4a16.json
.../E=512,N=80,device_name=NVIDIA_A100-SXM4-40GB,dtype=int4_w4a16_down.json
```

Weight loading and memory allocation succeed:

```text
Load weight end. type=Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration, mem usage=19.19 GB.
Load weight end. type=Qwen4ExpForCausalLMMTP, mem usage=1.78 GB.
Mamba Cache is allocated.
KV Cache is allocated. #tokens: 612672, K size: 3.51 GB, V size: 3.51 GB.
```

Then capture reaches bs=16 and crashes in QSA sparse attention:

```text
Capture target verify CUDA graph begin. backend=full, num_tokens_per_req=4, bs=[...]
Capturing batches (bs=16 avail_mem=2.43 GB): 0%| 0/12 [00:52<?, ?it/s]
...
qwen_sparse_attn_backend.py -> _forward_paged_attention -> flash_attn_varlen_func
flash_attn/cute/interface.py -> _flash_attn_fwd
cutlass._mlir...MLIRError: Operation creation failed:
error: unknown: unable to compute crd2idx with
  '!cute.layout<"(?):(?{i64 div=8})">' and '!cute.coord<"((?,?))">'
```

The traceback starts in the Qwen4Exp target-verify CUDA-graph path and passes through `QwenSparseAttnBackend.forward_extend`, so the second failure is independent of the MoE backend that successfully loaded.

### Workarounds considered

- `--moe-runner-backend triton` avoids the exact Marlin failure, but exposes the second QSA/FA-CuTe failure.
- Disabling decode CUDA graph may bypass capture, but has not yet been tested here and is expected to reduce decode performance.
- The official Flash-Next cookbook currently verifies H200/B200/B300/GB300/MI350X/MI355X; A100 and community W4A16 are outside the verified matrix, so this report is mainly about making the failure actionable and determining whether A100 TP4 can be supported or should fail fast with a clearer compatibility message.

### Request

1. Confirm whether `CompressedTensorsWNA16MarlinMoEMethod` can support the TP4-sharded Flash-Next expert GEMM shape (`prob_n = 320`), or whether it should fall back to Triton automatically for invalid Marlin shapes.
2. For the Triton MoE + QSA path, determine whether A100/SM80 can use classic FA2 for QSA instead of `flash_attn.cute`, or whether A100 should be explicitly unsupported/preflighted for this day-0 model.
3. If known, advice on the best supported A100 configuration for this W4A16 checkpoint, even if it requires disabling CUDA graphs.
